facet_contributions.boundaries: 机制部分主要依赖作者引用的既往研究和推测，本研究本身未进行体外或体内机制验证；需结合其他研究确认这些代谢物在肺癌免疫微环境中的具体作用。
facet_contributions.contribution: 提出了潜在的机制线索：SCFAs可能通过调节免疫细胞（如巨噬细胞、树突状细胞、T细胞）的功能来促进抗肿瘤免疫（引用文献支持SCFAs的免疫调节作用）；而对甲酚和某些酮类可能具有细胞毒性或抑制Th1型免疫反应。同时指出菌群结构本身并未显示出差异，强调了代谢功能的独立性。
facet_contributions.possible_uses: 用于构建‘代谢物-宿主免疫互作’的机制框架；解释为何菌群组成相似但治疗效果不同（功能异质性）；讨论特定代谢途径（如酪氨酸分解产对甲酚，糖发酵产SCFAs）在免疫微环境中的作用。

review_planning_B.planning_summary: 该论文提供了一个关于“肠道微生物组代谢功能”而非“菌群组成”影响免疫治疗反应的实证案例。对于综述而言，其核心价值在于支持‘代谢表型比物种丰度更能反映功能性状态’的观点，并提供了具体的代谢物列表（SCFAs有益，某些酮类和芳香族化合物有害）作为机制讨论的素材。由于样本量小且为相关性研究，它适合作为假设生成或背景支持的证据，而非确证性结论。
scope_interpretation_cautions: 样本量极小（n=11），结果具有高度情境依赖性，不能外推至所有NSCLC患者或所有免疫治疗药物。
十三烷仅在EPs中检出，这一发现需谨慎解读，可能是特异性标志物也可能是噪声。
作者声称的‘首次’检测NSCLC肠道代谢组与免疫反应关联，应理解为在该特定队列和方法下的初步发现，而非领域内的绝对首创。
16S测序未显示差异，但代谢组学显示差异，提示菌群组成与功能可能存在解耦，解读时需强调功能层面的重要性。
补充材料（Figure S1, Tables S1/S2）缺失，无法独立验证原始数据和聚类细节。

study_summary_A.approach: 1. 队列定义：纳入11例晚期NSCLC患者，二线使用nivolumab。根据临床结局定义两组：早期进展者（EPs, n=4, PFS<3个月）和长期响应者（LRs, n=7, PFS>12个月）。 2. 样本采集与处理：收集基线粪便样本。 3. 多组学分析： - 微生物组结构：提取DNA，扩增16S rRNA V3-V4区，Illumina MiSeq测序，使用QIIME流程进行OTU聚类和分析。 - 挥发性代谢物：采用固相微萃取-气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS/SPME）检测VOCs。 - 非挥发性代谢物：采用核磁共振氢谱（1H-NMR）检测水溶性代谢物。 4. 统计分析：对GC-MS和NMR数据进行低水平融合（low-level data fusion），进行块缩放（block scaling）后执行主成分分析（PCA）以观察组间分离。使用Mann-Whitney U检验比较单变量代谢物的显著性差异。

contribution_and_limits.contribution: 提供了初步证据，表明肠道微生物组的代谢功能（而非菌群组成）与NSCLC患者对抗PD-1治疗的反应相关；识别出特定的代谢物组合（SCFAs vs. 酮类/烷烃）作为潜在的反应预测指标。
contribution_and_limits.limits: 样本量极小（n=11），且为单中心研究；缺乏外部验证队列；未阐明具体的因果机制（即这些代谢物如何直接调节免疫系统）；16S测序分辨率有限，无法确定产生特定代谢物的具体菌种；部分补充材料（图表）缺失。

key_findings.conditions: NSCLC患者基线粪便样本，对比早期进展者（EPs）与长期响应者（LRs）
key_findings.finding: 16S rRNA测序显示，基于Bray-Curtis距离的菌群结构分析未在EPs和LRs之间发现显著的聚类或分类群丰度差异。
PCA得分图显示EPs和LRs沿PC1轴明显分离。LRs组主要由短链脂肪酸（丙酸、丁酸、乙酸、戊酸）、氨基酸（赖氨酸）和烟酸主导；EPs组主要由烷烃（十三烷、十二烷）、甲基酮（2-戊酮、2-辛酮）、醛类和对甲酚主导。

key_findings.conditions: 单变量统计检验（Mann-Whitney U test）
key_findings.finding: 丙酸（p=0.016）、赖氨酸（p=0.032）、烟酸（p=0.016）在LRs中显著高于EPs；十三烷（p=0.032）、2-戊酮（p=0.016）和对甲酚（p=0.016）在EPs中显著高于LRs。十三烷仅在EPs中检测到，LRs中缺失。

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: 尽管免疫检查点抑制剂（ICIs）有效，但仅20-30%的患者能获得长期益处。现有的生物标志物（如PD-L1表达、TMB）存在局限性。本研究试图回答：肠道微生物组的代谢谱（metabolome）是否能在基线阶段预测NSCLC患者对nivolumab的治疗反应？
study_summary_A.research_scope: 11例接受二线抗PD-1免疫检查点抑制剂（nivolumab）治疗的IV期非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者；聚焦基线粪便样本中的肠道微生物组代谢产物（挥发性有机化合物VOCs和非挥发性代谢物）。
study_summary_A.work_summary: 该研究旨在探索肠道微生物组代谢特征是否能预测NSCLC患者对免疫治疗的反应。研究招募了11名接受nivolumab治疗的患者，根据无进展生存期（PFS）将其分为早期进展者（EPs，PFS<3个月）和长期响应者（LRs，PFS>12个月）。通过GC-MS/SPME和1H-NMR技术对基线粪便样本进行非靶向代谢组学分析，并结合16S rRNA测序评估菌群结构。结果显示，虽然菌群结构在两组间无显著差异，但整合的代谢组学数据能清晰区分EPs和LRs。LRs的特征是高水平的短链脂肪酸（SCFAs）、赖氨酸和烟酸，而EPs则表现为高浓度的2-戊酮、十三烷和对甲酚。这表明肠道微生物组的代谢功能而非单纯的菌群组成可能与免疫治疗反应相关。

supplement_gap_material.auxiliary_material: The authors discuss the gut-lung axis theory, hypothesizing that fecal metabolites may systemically influence lung immunity despite the lack of direct intratumoral measurement. They report that 16S rRNA metagenomics did not distinguish responders from non-responders, whereas metabolomic profiling did, suggesting functional metabolic status may be more informative than taxonomic composition. The study utilized GC–MS/SPME for volatile metabolites and 1H-NMR for non-volatile metabolites. Inosine was not among the metabolites reported or discussed in the provided text.
supplement_gap_material.outline_action: Use this study to support the background argument that gut microbiota metabolites correlate with ICI response in NSCLC, specifically citing the fecal SCFA quantification methods and values. Clearly distinguish these fecal findings from the gap's requirement for intratumoral data in the review text. Highlight the methodological approach (NMR/GC-MS) as a reference for metabolite quantification while noting the sample type limitation. Do not present these fecal concentrations as surrogate markers for intratumoral concentrations without additional evidence.
supplement_gap_material.remaining_gap: The specific requirement for absolute concentrations of inosine and SCFAs inside the human tumour microenvironment (intratumoral tissue) is not addressed, as this study only analyzed fecal samples. Paired tumor tissue and serum metabolomics were not performed. The cohort size is small (n=11), and the study does not establish a direct mechanistic link between fecal metabolites and intratumoral immune activity, relying instead on the gut-lung axis hypothesis.
supplement_gap_material.useful_material: This study prospectively measured absolute concentrations of specific short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) including propionic, butyric, acetic, and valeric acids in fecal samples from 11 NSCLC patients treated with nivolumab, reporting quantification in µmol/g (e.g., propionic acid median 7.14 µmol/g in long responders vs 2.56 µmol/g in early progressors). The authors correlated these fecal metabolite levels with clinical response (progression-free survival), finding that higher SCFA concentrations were associated with long-term benefit, while volatile organic compounds like 2-pentanone and tridecane were associated with early progression.

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Supports arguments for why studying microbiome-ICI interactions requires more complex, human-relevant models than traditional methods, justifying the focus on organoids in the broader review.
broader_review_uses.material: Comparison of 2D cell lines, animal xenografts, and organoids, highlighting that animal models lack human-specific immune/microbiome structures and 2D cultures lack tissue context.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Contextualize the need for novel modeling systems

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Offers concrete examples of therapeutic interventions targeting the microbiome, which can be discussed in the context of how organoid models might be used to optimize these therapies for individual patients.
broader_review_uses.material: References to FMT, probiotic administration (Bifidobacterium), and dietary changes improving ICI outcomes in clinical and preclinical settings.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Provide examples of successful microbiome manipulation strategies

broader_review_uses.connection_to_review: Highlights the current technological barriers in the field, providing a balanced view of the potential and limitations of using organoids to study microbiome-ICI interactions.
broader_review_uses.material: Discussion of difficulties in culturing live bacteria with tissues, oxygen gradients, and maintaining immune cell viability in organoids.
broader_review_uses.purpose: Identify technical challenges in microbiome-organoid integration

facet_contributions.boundaries: The review notes that biomarkers are cohort-dependent and no single species is universally predictive. It does not provide causal proof for all observed associations, only correlations and some mechanistic hypotheses.
facet_contributions.contribution: Summarizes clinical evidence showing that specific gut microbiota profiles (e.g., Akkermansia, Bifidobacterium) and higher diversity are associated with better response rates to ICIs in solid tumors like melanoma and NSCLC. It details interventions like FMT that restore responsiveness.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Use to establish the clinical baseline of microbiome-ICI correlation in solid tumors. Cite to support the existence of a microbiome effect on ICI efficacy before discussing mechanistic models.

facet_contributions.boundaries: The mechanistic explanations are largely derived from cited studies or theoretical frameworks; the review itself does not perform new mechanistic experiments. The link between specific metabolites and specific immune cell subsets in organoids is presented as an emerging capability rather than a settled consensus.
facet_contributions.contribution: Describes proposed mechanisms such as antigen mimicry, pattern recognition receptor activation, and metabolite-mediated immune modulation (e.g., SCFAs promoting T-cell differentiation). It highlights how immune-reactive organoids can be used to test these mechanisms ex vivo.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Use to explain the biological plausibility of microbiome effects on ICI. Use the organoid methodology section to illustrate how these mechanisms can be studied in a controlled, human-relevant setting, contrasting with animal model limitations.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review serves as a critical background source for understanding why advanced in vitro models like immune-reactive organoids are necessary to study microbiome-ICI interactions. It provides a curated summary of clinical associations between specific gut bacteria/metabolites and ICI efficacy in solid tumors, which helps contextualize the biological phenomena that these novel models aim to replicate. It also offers a comparative analysis of modeling platforms, justifying the shift towards organoid-based approaches for mechanistic studies.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative synthesis, not a systematic meta-analysis; clinical associations should be treated as reported trends rather than definitive causal rules.
Organoid data cited are from specific proof-of-concept studies; generalizations about organoid performance should acknowledge the variability and ongoing development of these platforms.
The term 'immune-reactive organoids' encompasses different methodologies (endogenous retention vs. co-culture); distinctions between these approaches should be maintained when applying findings.

study_summary_A.approach: As a review article, the approach involves a structured synthesis of literature rather than new empirical experimentation. The authors systematically: 1) Summarize clinical trial data associating specific gut microbiota profiles with ICI response in solid tumors; 2) Compare the advantages and limitations of traditional 2D cell lines, animal xenografts, and emerging 3D organoid models; 3) Detail the methodologies for generating immune-reactive organoids (endogenous retention vs. autologous co-culture); 4) Review selected studies demonstrating the application of these organoids in testing microbial metabolites and immunotherapies; 5) Discuss future perspectives and challenges in integrating microbiome components into organoid cultures.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive synthesis of clinical evidence linking gut microbiota to ICI response in solid tumors, identifying key taxa and metabolic pathways involved.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Does not present new primary data; relies on summarizing existing heterogeneous clinical studies where biomarkers are not yet standardized.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Critically evaluates the limitations of current preclinical models (2D and animal) and advocates for immune-reactive organoids as a bridge between reductionist models and complex in vivo systems.
contribution_and_limits.limits: The discussion of organoid capabilities is largely prospective or based on a limited set of recent proof-of-concept studies; widespread validation and standardization of these models are still ongoing challenges.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Outlines specific methodologies for creating immune-reactive organoids (endogenous vs. co-culture) and highlights their potential for personalized medicine and mechanistic dissection of microbiome-immune interactions.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Technical challenges such as maintaining viable immune cells and live bacteria in long-term culture, as well as the cost and scalability of patient-derived organoids, are acknowledged but not fully resolved within the scope of this review.

key_findings.conditions: Clinical association studies across melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, and other solid tumors treated with ICIs
key_findings.finding: Higher gut microbiome diversity and richness are generally associated with improved clinical response to ICIs. Specific taxa such as Akkermansia muciniphila, Bifidobacterium spp., Prevotella spp., and Ruminococcaceae are enriched in responders, while Proteobacteria and certain Firmicutes are often higher in non-responders. However, no single biomarker is consistently predictive across all cohorts.

key_findings.conditions: Mechanistic studies involving microbial metabolites and immune modulation
key_findings.finding: Microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and inosine can modulate systemic immunity, promoting T-cell differentiation and enhancing the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitors. For example, Bacteroides pseudolongum-derived inosine enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy via UBA6 inhibition.

Immune-reactive organoids preserve patient-specific heterogeneity and allow for the study of spatial immune infiltration and drug response. Co-culture systems with autologous immune cells have shown high predictive accuracy (e.g., 85% in melanoma) for clinical ICI outcomes compared to 2D cultures or animal models.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: The review addresses the gap between clinical observations of microbiome-ICI associations and the lack of robust, human-relevant preclinical models to mechanistically dissect these interactions. It questions how current models fail to capture the complexity of the tumor-immune-microbiome axis and proposes immune-reactive organoids as a solution to predict patient-specific responses and understand underlying mechanisms.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The review focuses on the intersection of cancer immunotherapy, specifically immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in solid tumors, and the gut microbiome. It evaluates various preclinical models, with a primary emphasis on immune-reactive tumor organoids as a platform to study these interactions.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This paper is a narrative review that argues for the utility of immune-reactive tumor organoids in deciphering how the microbiome influences cancer immunity and response to immunotherapies. It begins by outlining the clinical evidence linking gut microbiota composition to ICI outcomes in solid tumors, summarizing key findings from multiple clinical trials regarding specific bacterial taxa and metabolites. The review then critiques existing modeling systems (2D cultures and animal models), highlighting their limitations in capturing human-specific immune-microbiome-tumor dynamics. It proposes immune-reactive organoids—created either by retaining endogenous immune cells or co-culturing autologous immune cells with tumor organoids—as a superior ex vivo platform. The authors discuss recent experimental data using these organoid systems to test microbial metabolites and checkpoint blockade efficacy, assessing their validity for personalized medicine and mechanistic insight.

facet_contributions.contribution: Details specific molecular mechanisms: e.g., PSA from B. fragilis polarizing Th1; Inosine from B. pseudolongum/A. muciniphila activating A2AR signaling; SCFAs promoting memory T cells; F. nucleatum inducing PD-L1 or MDSC recruitment via succinate/EZH2. Also explains how antibiotics disrupt these pathways (e.g., reducing DC function, altering cytokine profiles like IL-8/CCL23).
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Provides mechanistic depth for 'how' microbiota affects immunity. Useful for explaining pathways like T cell differentiation, antigen presentation, and metabolic modulation. Can illustrate how antibiotics mechanistically impair these processes.

facet_contributions.boundaries: Data is primarily from retrospective cohort studies and meta-analyses; confounding factors (severity of infection, patient health status) cannot be fully ruled out. Does not prove that dysbiosis *causes* the poor outcome, though mechanistic plausibility is discussed.
facet_contributions.contribution: Synthesizes retrospective clinical data showing that antibiotic use (especially broad-spectrum and fluoroquinolones) within 30-60 days of ICI initiation is associated with reduced PFS and OS in NSCLC, RCC, melanoma, and other solid tumors.
facet_contributions.possible_uses: Supports the argument that antibiotic exposure is a negative prognostic factor for ICI efficacy in solid tumors. Helps define the clinical scope of the 'antibiotic effect'.

review_planning_B.planning_summary: This review serves as a high-level conceptual map for understanding how gut microbiota modulates ICI efficacy in solid tumors. It provides detailed mechanistic explanations for both beneficial and detrimental microbial effects, categorizes key bacterial taxa and metabolites, and summarizes clinical evidence regarding antibiotic interference. It is particularly useful for explaining the biological basis of ICI resistance/sensitivity and for contextualizing the impact of concomitant medications like antibiotics.
scope_interpretation_cautions: The review is a narrative synthesis; do not treat its summaries of clinical data as primary evidence or meta-analytic results.
Mechanistic claims are often based on preclinical models; distinguish between observed correlations in humans and demonstrated mechanisms in mice.
The 'critical window' for antibiotic impact is an observation from retrospective studies; exact durations may vary by study and antibiotic class.
Do not generalize findings from specific cancers (e.g., CRC-specific F. nucleatum effects) to all solid tumors without noting context-dependence.

study_summary_A.approach: As a narrative review, the authors systematically summarize and integrate findings from existing literature (citing numerous primary studies and meta-analyses). They organize the content into sections covering: 1) Mechanisms of GM shaping immune responses (local and systemic); 2) Specific immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive microbes and their products; 3) The negative impact of antibiotics on ICI responses (clinical data and mechanistic insights); 4) The potential positive impact of targeted antibiotic use; and 5) Critical perspectives and future directions. The approach relies on interpreting and connecting disparate experimental and clinical observations rather than conducting new primary research or a systematic meta-analysis with predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Provides a comprehensive synthesis of mechanistic pathways linking GM to ICI efficacy, categorizing immunostimulatory and immunosuppressive microbes and their molecular targets (e.g., STING, TLRs, metabolites).
contribution_and_limits.limits: As a narrative review, it does not perform a quantitative meta-analysis; conclusions are based on qualitative synthesis of cited studies, which vary in design and quality.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Highlights the clinical relevance of antibiotic timing and spectrum, emphasizing a 'critical window' of vulnerability for ICI efficacy.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Most clinical evidence cited is retrospective; causal relationships between specific dysbiosis patterns and ICI resistance are often inferred rather than proven in randomized trials.

contribution_and_limits.contribution: Discusses the dual role of antibiotics (negative general impact vs. positive targeted impact), offering nuanced perspectives for clinical decision-making.
contribution_and_limits.limits: Recommendations for targeted antibiotic use are largely based on preclinical models or small-scale human studies; large-scale prospective validation is needed.

key_findings.finding: Specific gut microbial taxa (e.g., Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia muciniphila) are associated with favorable ICI responses through mechanisms involving T cell priming, DC activation, and metabolite production (e.g., inosine, SCFAs).

key_findings.conditions: Antibiotic exposure within 30-60 days before or shortly after ICI initiation
key_findings.finding: Antibiotic use is consistently associated with poorer clinical outcomes (reduced PFS and OS) across multiple solid tumor types, likely due to dysbiosis impairing immune surveillance.

key_findings.finding: Antibiotics targeting specific pathobionts (e.g., F. nucleatum in CRC) or stress-induced dysbiosis can improve ICI outcomes by reducing immunosuppressive signals or generating neoantigens.

study_summary_A.problem_or_question: To understand the complex relationship between gut microbiota composition, antibiotic use, and the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in cancer patients, specifically addressing mechanisms of resistance and potential therapeutic interventions.
study_summary_A.research_scope: The review focuses on the interplay between gut microbiota (GM), antibiotic treatments, and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in patients with solid tumors. It covers mechanisms of GM modulation of systemic and intratumoral immunity, the impact of antibiotics on ICI efficacy across various cancer types (e.g., melanoma, NSCLC, RCC, CRC), and potential strategies for microbiome modulation.
study_summary_A.work_summary: This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on how the gut microbiome influences the efficacy of ICIs (anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, anti-CTLA-4) in cancer therapy. It details the biological mechanisms by which specific microbial taxa and their metabolites shape host immune responses, including T cell differentiation and activation of dendritic cells. The review also critically evaluates the negative clinical impact of antibiotic-induced dysbiosis on ICI outcomes, highlighting a critical time window for antibiotic exposure. Furthermore, it discusses the paradoxical positive effects of targeting specific pathogenic bacteria with antibiotics and proposes future directions for personalized microbiome-based interventions to improve immunotherapy response.

studies.proposed_use: 用于论证微生物预测签名的“治疗方案特异性”，说明针对联合免疫（CICB）训练的菌株模型无法外推至抗 PD-1 单药，支持综述中按治疗策略分层解析微生物标志物的观点。
提供 mCRPC 队列中 A. muciniphila 与 ICI 响应负向关联的反例，论证既往内分泌治疗史可重塑菌群 - 疗效关系，支撑按癌种与治疗背景分层解析标志物的观点。
提供胃癌队列中乳酸杆菌丰度与 ICI 单药及联合治疗响应正相关的实证，展示不同治疗方案下微生物特征的特异性差异，支撑按治疗策略分层解析标志物的观点。
提供粪便短链脂肪酸（特别是丙酸）浓度与实体瘤 ICI 无进展生存期独立相关的定量临床证据，同时提示其作为系统性代谢物指标在追溯具体产菌物种及建立组织内因果链条时的局限性。
详述 SCFAs 在抗 PD-1 与抗 CTLA-4 背景下呈现相反预后效应的矛盾数据，警示代谢物效应的情境依赖性，解释为何粪便/血清浓度难以直接外推为组织内因果机制。
详述短链脂肪酸在抗 PD-1 与抗 CTLA-4 背景下呈现相反预后效应的矛盾数据，警示代谢物效应的情境依赖性，解释为何粪便/血清浓度难以直接外推为组织内因果机制。
展示通过比较基因组学锁定有效菌株特有代谢通路（如乙酸合成、维生素合成）的方法论路径，明确此类基于基因存在性的功能注释仍属预测性证据，需结合后续体外或体内实验完成因果验证。
展示宏基因组功能通路（如 L-异亮氨酸合成）与宏转录组表达谱联合分析预测 PFS 的路径，明确基因存在性注释的预测属性及需转录活性验证的方法学边界。
揭示基于肠型分层识别生物标志物的探索性框架，指出跨队列验证时因肿瘤类型混杂及缺乏非响应者对照导致的泛化瓶颈，支撑综述关于标准化多中心前瞻性验证必要性的判断。
提出“功能趋同”理论框架解释跨队列分类学不一致现象，结合文献计量演变揭示从机制探索向临床干预转型的现状，支撑对标准化多中心前瞻性验证必要性的判断。

chapter.purpose: 使读者掌握预测 ICI 疗效的核心微生物特征清单，理解分类学特征与代谢物在预测效力上的差异，明确当前生物标志物研究的证据层级（观察性关联 vs. 定量验证），并识别限制其临床转化的关键方法学与生物学边界。
chapter.scope: 肠道微生物群通过特定的分类学特征（门/属/种/株）与代谢物谱（SCFAs、肌苷等）系统性调节实体瘤 ICI 疗效，但现有证据呈现高度的情境依赖性（癌种、治疗方案、宿主背景）。观察性关联已确立特定菌群与代谢物的预后价值，而定量代谢组学与菌株分辨率研究正推动生物标志物从“物种丰度”向“功能通路”演进；然而，人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度的缺失及跨队列泛化能力的不足，限制了其作为独立临床决策工具的转化就绪度。
substantive_threads: 特定菌属/种的富集与 ICI 响应相关，但效应方向高度依赖癌种与治疗策略，单一通用标志物难以成立。
粪便与血浆中的 SCFAs 及肌苷浓度提供定量预后信号，但缺乏肿瘤组织内绝对浓度数据，限制机制外推与因果推断。
菌株水平宏基因组分析揭示种内功能异质性，功能通路预测效力优于单一物种丰度，但实验性功能验证仍待完成。
现有证据支持微生物组作为 ICI 疗效的预测维度，但转化就绪度受限于方法学异质性、因果链条未闭合及缺乏大型 III 期验证。

chapter.title: 微生物特征：预测 ICI 反应的菌分类群与代谢物
chapter.transition_logic: 承接 CH01 确立的临床关联（抗生素时机、FMT 试验），本章具体化‘哪些微生物’在起作用，为 CH03 的机制阐释（‘如何起作用’）提供物质基础；强调分类学标志物的异质性将自然引出 CH03 对功能通路和分子机制的深入探讨。

chapter_plan.reader_objective: 使读者掌握预测 ICI 疗效的核心微生物特征清单，理解分类学特征与代谢物在预测效力上的差异，明确当前生物标志物研究的证据层级（观察性关联 vs. 定量验证），并识别限制其临床转化的关键方法学与生物学边界。
chapter_plan.thesis: 肠道微生物群通过特定的分类学特征（门/属/种/株）与代谢物谱（SCFAs、肌苷等）系统性调节实体瘤 ICI 疗效，但现有证据呈现高度的情境依赖性（癌种、治疗方案、宿主背景）。观察性关联已确立特定菌群与代谢物的预后价值，而定量代谢组学与菌株分辨率研究正推动生物标志物从“物种丰度”向“功能通路”演进；然而，人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度的缺失及跨队列泛化能力的不足，限制了其作为独立临床决策工具的转化就绪度。

concrete_studies.conditions: 接受 ICI 治疗的实体瘤患者（黑色素瘤为主，含外部队列 n=364）；比较 CICB 与单药方案下的预测性能。
concrete_studies.finding: 在黑色素瘤及外部荟萃分析中，菌株水平微生物特征显著优于物种水平预测 ICI 反应（AUC 0.85 vs 0.67）；且该特征仅适用于 CICB 方案，在抗 PD-1 单药队列中预测力降至随机水平。

concrete_studies.conditions: 晚期 NSCLC 患者（n=270 基线粪便样本）；比较不同一线治疗方案（NIC vs PC）下的微生物组 - 生存期关联。
concrete_studies.finding: 在 NSCLC 新辅助化疗+ICI 治疗背景下，Fusicatenibacter 和 Butyricicoccus 高丰度与更长 OS 相关，且该关联在 NIC（纳武利尤单抗 + 伊匹木单抗）臂中显著，而在 PC（培美曲塞 + 铂类）臂中较弱。

concrete_studies.conditions: 接受 ICI 治疗的多种实体瘤患者（黑色素瘤、NSCLC、RCC 等）；基于已发表队列的定性综合。
concrete_studies.finding: 综述汇总显示，Faecalibacterium、Akkermansia muciniphila、Bifidobacterium spp.在多种实体瘤中与良好 ICI 预后相关；而 Bacteroidales 富集常与非响应或毒性增加相关，但具体效应因癌种而异。

units.evidence_conditions_limits: 证据条件：主要基于人类临床队列的观察性关联。局限：缺乏大规模前瞻性随机对照试验确证因果链条；跨队列泛化能力受限于训练集分布与批次效应；部分阳性信号可能反映治疗后的生态位重塑而非基线预测因子。
units.material_supported_relations_conditions_: 分类学特征与 ICI 疗效的关联多为回顾性或前瞻性观察性数据，存在残余混杂（如抗生素使用、饮食、地理因素）。不同研究使用的测序平台（16S vs. 宏基因组）、生信管道及临床终点定义（ORR vs PFS vs OS）导致直接比较困难。效应方向的情境依赖性提示不能将某一菌属简单归类为普适性“有益”或“有害”标志物。
units.ordered_development: 首先列举跨癌种中反复出现的阳性与阴性标志物，随后引入治疗方案（联合免疫检查点阻断 CICB vs. 抗 PD-1 单药）对菌群效应的修饰作用，最后指出不同研究间结果不一致的根源在于治疗背景与人群异质性。
units.substantive_point: 特定菌属/种的富集与 ICI 响应相关，但效应方向高度依赖癌种与治疗策略，单一通用标志物难以成立。
units.transition: 尽管分类学特征提供了初步的预后信号，但其预测效力受限于物种水平的功能模糊性。为突破这一瓶颈，研究正转向定量代谢物分析与菌株分辨率解析，以捕捉更精确的功能输出。

concrete_studies.conditions: 日本单中心实体瘤患者（n=52）；基线粪便与血浆样本；比较响应者与非响应者的 SCFA 浓度。
concrete_studies.finding: 在 52 例接受 PD-1 抑制剂治疗的实体瘤患者中，响应者粪便丙酸中位浓度为 172.6 μmol/g（非响应者 103.6 μmol/g）；多变量 Cox 模型确认高粪便丙酸浓度是较长 PFS 的独立保护因子（HR 0.07, 95% CI 0.03–0.19）。

concrete_studies.conditions: 晚期 NSCLC 患者（n=11）；基线粪便样本；对比 LRs（PFS>12 个月）与 EPs（PFS<3 个月）的挥发性有机化合物与水溶性代谢物。
concrete_studies.finding: 在 11 例二线 nivolumab 治疗的 NSCLC 患者中，长期响应者（LRs）粪便中丙酸、丁酸、乙酸、戊酸及烟酸水平显著高于早期进展者（EPs）；整合代谢组学 PCA 模型清晰区分两组，但 16S 测序未显示显著聚类差异。

concrete_studies.conditions: 跨癌种机制探讨；聚焦肌苷的生化特性、受体结合（A2AR）及 UBA6 抑制路径。
concrete_studies.finding: 综述指出肌苷由肠道菌群（如 Bifidobacterium pseudolongum）产生，可通过抑制肿瘤细胞 UBA6 增强 ICI 疗效；但明确指出人类肿瘤组织中肌苷的空间重分布与定量浓度数据目前缺失，临床关联多基于动物模型或血清间接推断。

units.evidence_conditions_limits: 证据条件：定量代谢组学（LC-MS/MS、NMR、GC-MS）提供绝对浓度单位（μmol/g 或μM）。局限：多数研究未进行配对肿瘤组织活检代谢组学分析；代谢物半衰期短、采样窗口敏感；缺乏标准化前处理流程导致跨实验室可比性差。
units.material_supported_relations_conditions_: 代谢物浓度与 ICI 预后的关联多为横断面或短期纵向观察，无法排除疾病状态或合并用药对代谢谱的即时干扰。粪便/血浆浓度虽具统计学显著性，但未能反映肿瘤微环境（TME）内的实际暴露水平；局部浓度缺失使得剂量 - 效应关系（如 SCFAs 的双向作用阈值）无法在人体中校准。
units.ordered_development: 报告系统循环与粪便代谢物的具体浓度值及其与生存期的统计关联，对比不同检测部位（粪便/血浆 vs. 肿瘤间质液）的数据缺口，阐明为何局部浓度缺失阻碍了代谢物介导机制的确证。
units.substantive_point: 粪便与血浆中的 SCFAs 及肌苷浓度提供定量预后信号，但缺乏肿瘤组织内绝对浓度数据，限制机制外推与因果推断。
units.transition: 定量代谢物证据揭示了功能输出的潜力，但物种水平的丰度仍无法完全解释个体差异。高分辨率宏基因组分析正揭示种内功能异质性，推动预测范式从“谁存在”向“能做什么”转变。

concrete_studies.conditions: CA209-538 试验发现队列（n=106）及六个外部公共队列（n=364）；深度鸟枪法宏基因组测序；比较科/属/种/株层级的预测性能。
concrete_studies.finding: 构建包含 1,397 个基因组的自定义菌株参考库后，菌株水平微生物丰度显著优于物种水平预测 ICI 反应（AUC 0.85 vs. 0.67）；正向关联菌株（如特定 Faecalibacterium）普遍拥有完整的乙酰辅酶 A 丁酸生成途径，而负向关联菌株缺失该通路。

concrete_studies.conditions: 转移性肾细胞癌患者（Pal et al. 临床试验）；评估含特定双歧杆菌的益生菌联合 ICI 的效果。
concrete_studies.finding: 综述指出特定益生菌干预（如 CBM588 含双歧杆菌）在 mRCC ICI 治疗中显著提升 PFS（从 2.5 个月增至 12.7 个月），但强调菌株特异性效应至关重要，且目前缺乏针对内源性关联菌株的实验性因果验证。

concrete_studies.conditions: 跨癌种机制与临床证据综合；聚焦功能通路预测优势与方法学挑战。
concrete_studies.finding: 综述强调微生物组功能通路（如 SCFA 合成、色氨酸代谢）比分类学组成更能稳定预测 ICI 结局；指出当前研究多依赖基因组注释推断功能，需结合宏转录组或代谢组确认实际转录活性与代谢通量。

units.evidence_conditions_limits: 证据条件：深度宏基因组测序结合自定义参考库实现菌株级定量；机器学习交叉验证支持泛化潜力。局限：功能注释依赖数据库完整性；缺乏配对转录组/蛋白组验证；临床前菌株定植实验未与人类基线队列严格匹配，外推需谨慎。
units.material_supported_relations_conditions_: 菌株分辨率提升了预测精度，但基因组存在性不等于实际表达或代谢活性。功能通路的富集多为计算预测，尚未在人类患者中通过代谢物补充或基因敲除实验验证其对 ICI 响应的直接因果贡献。种内功能异质性提示单一物种丰度可能掩盖关键菌株的拮抗或协同作用。
units.ordered_development: 展示菌株分辨率如何提升机器学习预测 AUC，列举关键功能基因簇（如乙酰辅酶 A 丁酸生成途径、UBA6 抑制相关通路），说明从基因组潜力到表型关联的逻辑链条，并指出体外/体内功能验证的缺口。
units.substantive_point: 菌株水平宏基因组分析揭示种内功能异质性，功能通路预测效力优于单一物种丰度，但实验性功能验证仍待完成。
units.transition: 分类学、代谢物定量与菌株功能证据共同勾勒出微生物组调节 ICI 疗效的多维图景，但证据强度的不均与转化障碍要求我们在综合时保持审慎，明确当前研究的适用边界与未来优先事项。

concrete_studies.conditions: 多种实体瘤 ICI 治疗背景；综合临床前与早期临床试验证据。
concrete_studies.finding: 综述总结指出，尽管特定微生物特征与 ICI 响应关联广泛报道，但缺乏统一的生物标志物签名；FMT 在难治性患者中展现概念验证潜力，但供体筛选、给药途径及长期安全性仍需大规模 RCT 确证。

concrete_studies.conditions: 多个独立 ICI 治疗队列的外部验证阶段；评估模型泛化能力与临床部署可行性。

units.ordered_development: 综合前述单元的证据层级，指出当前共识（抗生素管理可基于观察性数据提出建议，但 FMT 及代谢物干预需等待 III 期验证），强调标准化协议、多中心前瞻性队列及代谢物空间定量是跨越“相关性”至“功能性”的关键步骤。

The text also notes preclinical evidence that microbiome-derived inosine can enhance response to checkpoint blockade (184). useful_material: This prospective cohort study (n=52) measured quantitative concentrations of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in human plasma and fecal samples from patients with solid tumors treated with PD-1 inhibitors. The authors reported median concentrations in μmol/g for multiple SCFAs, linking them to immune checkpoint inhibitor outcomes. Specifically, fecal propionic acid concentrations were significantly higher in responders (median 172.6 μmol/g) compared to nonresponders (median 103.6 μmol/g), and high fecal propionic acid was independently associated with longer progression-free survival (multivariate HR, 0.07; 95% CI, 0.03-0.19). Plasma isovaleric acid was also significantly higher in responders (median 0.3 μmol/g) vs nonresponders (median 0.0 μmol/g) and associated with progression-free survival (HR, 0.38; 95% CI, 0.14-0.99). Other measured SCFAs included acetic, butyric, valeric, isobutyric, hydroangelic, caproic, and succinic acids in both matrices. This provides quantitative metabolite data in a systemic biofluid (plasma) correlated with ICI efficacy, addressing the 'serum' and 'quantitative data' aspects of the success criteria for SCFAs.

This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as microbiota-derived metabolites with biological relevance to T-cell differentiation and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) efficacy, citing proof-of-principle evidence for inosine in mice (Section 5.1).

The authors explicitly state that paired measurements of candidate metabolites, including SCFAs and amino-acid pools, in stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are currently lacking in the literature (Section 5.1).

Table 1 provides quantitative data on fecal SCFAs from human intervention studies (e.g., Ahmad et al. 2020; Kwok et al. 2024), though these were conducted in healthy adults without ICI therapy and measured stool rather than tumor concentrations.

Section 3 details challenges in exposure assessment and metabolite measurement, noting that urinary biomarkers exist for some compounds but direct tumor microenvironment quantification remains a methodological gap.

The review distinguishes between contextual microbiome-ICI evidence (where inosine/SCFAs are mentioned as affecting T-cell fitness) and direct NNS-ICI evidence, clarifying that metabolite-ICI links often derive from studies not testing the specific exposure of interest (Section 6.1).

This narrative review establishes a mechanistic framework (Microbiome → Metabolites → Immune Modulation → TME State → ICI Response) linking gut microbial metabolites to immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy. The authors detail short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) mechanisms, including G-protein-coupled receptor binding and histone deacetylase inhibition, and explain that SCFA immune outcomes are concentration-dependent and microenvironment-specific (e.g., physiological mucosal concentrations favor Treg induction, while tumor-inflamed environments may favor CD8+ T-cell enhancement). Crucially, the authors explicitly state that the concentration-response relationship for SCFAs in human tumor-bearing contexts has not been characterized. The text does not contain any mention of inosine.

examples.conditions: 动物模型：B16-F0黑色素瘤小鼠，ICI治疗前后对比；临床队列：22名接受Sintilimab（抗PD-1）治疗的实体瘤患者，基于肿瘤组织UBA6蛋白表达（IHC评分）分组；指标：肿瘤体积、生存率、总体响应率（ORR）、UBA6蛋白表达水平。
examples.finding: 在小鼠模型中，携带B16-F0肿瘤的野生型小鼠血浆肌苷水平高于无肿瘤小鼠，但在接受ICI（抗PD-1 + 抗CTLA-4）治疗后，血浆肌苷水平下降。在人类临床验证部分，研究纳入了22名接受抗PD-1治疗的不同实体瘤（食管癌、肺癌、胃癌、结肠癌等）患者，发现部分缓解（PR）或疾病稳定（SD）患者的肿瘤组织中UBA6蛋白表达水平显著低于疾病进展（PD）患者。低UBA6表达组的总体响应率（ORR）为50%，高UBA6表达组为17%。虽然本研究未直接报告这22例患者血浆肌苷的具体浓度范围，但证实了UBA6低表达（模拟肌苷抑制效果）与良好ICI疗效正相关。
examples.use_in_review: 补充说明肌苷在动物模型中的变化趋势及临床样本中UBA6表达与疗效的关系，作为肌苷-UBA6轴的临床相关性佐证。

question_material.explanation: 该研究通过代谢组学筛选和临床队列分析，确立了血浆肌苷水平与免疫检查点阻断（ICI）疗效的正相关性。机制上，肌苷并非仅作为能量来源或作用于免疫细胞，而是直接进入肿瘤细胞，抑制泛素激活酶UBA6的活性。UBA6的抑制导致肿瘤细胞内FAT10依赖的抗原加工和炎症信号通路改变，上调MHC-I类分子表达和干扰素反应基因，从而增强肿瘤内在免疫原性，使其对T细胞介导的细胞毒性更敏感。在临床上，肿瘤细胞中UBA6的高表达预测了较差的ICI疗效，而低UBA6表达则与更好的生存期和响应率相关，提示肌苷或其类似物可能通过靶向UBA6来克服ICI耐药。

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: 1. Cite this meta-analysis as evidence of the current lack of completed Phase III data in peer-reviewed literature up to late 2024. 2. Perform a direct, current search of ClinicalTrials.gov and WHO ICTRP using terms 'microbiome', 'FMT', 'probiotic', 'Phase III', 'immune checkpoint inhibitor', and 'solid tumor' to identify any ongoing or recently completed trials not yet published. 3. Cross-reference any identified registry records with the studies included in this meta-analysis to ensure no duplication or missed data. 4. If no Phase III trials are found in registries, use this paper's conclusion ('larger-scale RCTs... are required') to substantiate the claim of absence.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this meta-analysis confirms the absence of completed large-scale Phase III RCTs in the published literature and searched registries up to September 2024, it does not rule out ongoing Phase III trials that have not yet reported results or were not captured in the search. The success criterion requires confirming absence through registry searches; this paper reports doing so, but a direct, current verification of ClinicalTrials.gov for 'Phase III' status trials (ongoing or completed without publication) remains necessary to fully close the gap.

useful_material.content: The meta-analysis searched ClinicalTrials.gov, chictr.org, and major oncology conference abstracts up to September 30, 2024, identifying 10 studies (164 patients). Among these, 5 were Phase I, 4 were Phase II–III, and 1 unspecified. Only 3 were RCTs (Spreafico et al. Phase 2/3, Glitza et al. Phase 1, Dizman et al. Phase 1). No completed large-scale Phase III RCTs reporting primary efficacy outcomes (OS/PFS/ORR) were identified in the included literature.
useful_material.relevance: Directly addresses the gap question by reporting the absence of completed large-scale Phase III RCTs in the searched literature and registries up to the search date.

useful_material.content: The authors conclude that 'larger-scale randomized controlled trials with long-term follow-up are required to confirm and optimize treatment protocols' and note 'the absence of randomized controlled trials was notable' (referring to large/definitive trials).
useful_material.relevance: Supports the confirmation of absence criterion by explicitly stating the field's need for such trials, implying they do not currently exist in a completed, reportable state.

useful_material.content: Pooled ORR was 43% across included studies (mostly Phase I/II). In the three included RCTs, heterogeneity increased, and the pooled Risk Ratio for ORR was 1.31 (95% CI: 0.58–2.98), crossing 1 (not statistically significant).
useful_material.relevance: Provides context on why Phase III data is needed; current RCT evidence is insufficient to establish efficacy, reinforcing the gap's importance.

useful_material: This review article systematically catalogs clinical trials of FMT combined with ICIs in solid tumors (Table 1), listing 29 trials with their phases, tumor types, and primary outcomes. All listed trials are Phase I, Phase Ib, Phase I/II, or Phase II; none are Phase III. The review explicitly states in Section 5.1 that 'large-scale, multi-center randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are essential to comprehensively evaluate the therapeutic potential of FMT in augmenting ICI therapy,' identifying this as a future research direction rather than completed evidence. The review discusses one randomized controlled trial (NCT03817125, SER-401) that was modified from a four-arm to a two-arm placebo-controlled design, but this was not Phase III and showed lower response rates in the intervention group versus placebo. The review provides mechanistic explanations for heterogeneous trial results (microbiota composition, metabolites, TME remodeling, signaling pathways) and outlines what future Phase III trials should measure (OS, PFS, ORR, quality of life).

This study explicitly characterizes the current evidence level for fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) as predominantly derived from early-phase, single-arm studies. It identifies a 2026 phase 2 randomized controlled trial (TACITO trial in metastatic renal cell carcinoma) as a pivotal step but notes it did not formally meet its primary endpoint. The authors conclude that large-scale phase 3 randomized controlled trials are critically needed and urgently prioritized to validate efficacy across tumor types, implying their absence in the published literature up to March 2026. The text also summarizes efficacy outcomes from available phase 1/2 trials (e.g., ORR of 80% in NSCLC, 75% in melanoma, 43% pooled in solid tumors) to contextualize the need for higher-level evidence.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Resolve the acquisition or judgment issue before making a scientific absence claim.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: What are the measured physiological concentrations of inosine and SCFAs inside the human tumour microenvironment correlating with ICI response?

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Search for primary metabolomics studies in ICI-treated cohorts that specifically report intratumoral or paired serum-stool-tumor concentrations of inosine and SCFAs, rather than reviews. Prioritize literature citing the inosine proof-of-principle study (reference 47 in this text) for human validation attempts. Investigate studies using spatial metabolomics or mass spectrometry imaging on tumor resections from immunotherapy patients.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: No prospective human studies reporting absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or specific SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients are identified in this material. The text confirms that such paired measurements are currently lacking in the literature it reviewed.
useful_material: The authors explicitly state that for most candidate microbiota-derived metabolites, including short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and amino-acid pools, paired measurements in stool, portal or peripheral blood, tumor tissue, and tumor interstitial fluid are lacking.

Inosine is identified as a proof-of-principle microbiota-derived metabolite that enhanced checkpoint-blockade efficacy and T-cell function in mice, though human intratumoral concentration data is not provided.

Contextual microbiome-ICI evidence is cited indicating that fiber-associated microbial functions, inosine, and SCFAs can affect T-cell differentiation and metabolic fitness, establishing biological relevance without providing the requested human concentration data.
The limitations section notes 'limited direct measurement of candidate metabolites within tumors' as a specific evidence gap.

Discussion on biomarker-based exposure assessment using liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) provides methodological context for how metabolite quantification might be approached, though applied here to sweeteners rather than tumor metabolites.

This study prospectively measured absolute concentrations of specific short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) including propionic, butyric, acetic, and valeric acids in fecal samples from 11 NSCLC patients treated with nivolumab, reporting quantification in µmol/g (e.g., propionic acid median 7.14 µmol/g in long responders vs 2.56 µmol/g in early progressors). The authors correlated these fecal metabolite levels with clinical response (progression-free survival), finding that higher SCFA concentrations were associated with long-term benefit, while volatile organic compounds like 2-pentanone and tridecane were associated with early progression.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this study to support the association between fecal SCFA levels (specifically propionate) and ICI clinical outcomes and intratumoral immune gene signatures. Cite the limitation that intratumoral metabolite concentrations were not directly quantified. Continue searching for studies that explicitly perform metabolomics on tumor biopsy samples paired with stool or serum in ICI-treated cohorts to fulfill the intratumoral quantification criterion.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The success criteria require absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or specific SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients. This study provides fecal SCFA concentrations and correlates them with outcomes and tumor gene expression, but it does not report the measured physiological concentrations of these metabolites inside the human tumor microenvironment. The specific intratumoral metabolite quantification remains unaddressed in the supplied text.
useful_material: This prospective study enrolled 39 patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (mNSCLC) treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) alone or with chemotherapy. The authors collected fecal and tumor samples prior to ICI initiation. Fecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFA) were measured by LC-MS/MS, and tumoral transcriptome profiling was performed via RNA sequencing. The study reported that high levels of fecal propionate correlated with significantly longer overall survival (p=0.02) and were increased in the high fiber diet group compared to the low fiber group. At the tumor level, RNA sequencing demonstrated upregulation of humoral and adaptive immune responses in the high fiber group. However, the text specifies fecal SCFA measurement and tumor transcriptomics; it does not explicitly report absolute concentrations of SCFAs or inosine within the tumor tissue itself.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as primary evidence for human strain-level metagenomic associations with ICI outcomes. Explicitly note the distinction between strain-level genomic association (fulfilled) and experimental functional validation (remaining gap). Search for subsequent studies that may have isolated the identified SGBs or gene clusters for gnotobiotic validation. Consider this material as a benchmark for strain-resolution methodology in future cohort comparisons.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this study establishes strain-level associations and predicts function via gene content, it does not provide experimental validation of the specific strain functions (e.g., isolating the beneficial E. coli strain to confirm causal mechanisms in vivo). The strain-level findings are currently limited to E. coli and F. prausnitzii due to abundance constraints, leaving other species (e.g., Bifidobacterium mentioned in the gap question) unaddressed at this resolution. Additionally, the primary cohort is lung cancer-specific; broader validation across tumor types for these specific strain markers is needed to confirm generalizability.
useful_material: This prospective human cohort study (n=54 metagenome, n=49 metabolome) utilized strain-level metagenomic resolution (StrainPhlAn, PanPhlAn) to distinguish specific strains of Escherichia coli and Faecalibacterium prausnitzii linked to ICI outcomes. It identified specific species-level genome bins (SGBs), such as F. prausnitzii SGB15342 and SGB15316_group, that were significantly enriched in the long-term benefit group compared to resistance. For E. coli, it distinguished harmful gene families (toxin-antitoxin, stress response) present in resistance/irAE groups from beneficial clusters absent in benefit groups. These strain-level genomic variations correlated with clinical phenotypes (efficacy and irAEs) independent of species-level abundance, directly addressing the requirement for strain-resolution linked to ICI outcomes.

This study analyzed four human fecal metagenomic cohorts (Ashray_2024, Lee_2022, Matson_2018, Frankel_2017) comprising patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The authors developed a deep learning model (BioP-VAE) using gene-level microbial abundance features (RPKM) and compared them against taxonomic abundance features at family, genus, species, and strain levels. The results showed that gene-level features outperformed all taxonomic levels for predicting ICI response (AUC 0.89 vs. strain-level AUC 0.72 in Ashray_2024). However, among taxonomic features, strain-level abundance provided better predictive performance for 12-month progression-free survival than species-level abundance (AUC 0.85 vs. 0.67). Feature attribution identified specific microbial genes and pathways (e.g., nitrilase in responders, lipoic acid metabolism in non-responders) and taxa (e.g., Ruminococcaceae, Desulfovibrionaceae) associated with outcomes, suggesting functional capacity is more predictive than taxonomy.

This study performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing on stool samples from 165 ICI-naive melanoma patients across five cohorts, integrated with 147 public samples. The authors identified a panel of species associated with responders, including Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum, Roseburia spp., and Akkermansia muciniphila, but explicitly stated no single species was a fully consistent biomarker across studies. While the methods section notes the use of bioBakery 3 which includes strain-level profiling tools (StrainPhlAn 3.0), the reported results focus on species-level relative abundances and functional potential (KEGG orthologs). The discussion explicitly highlights that microbial uniqueness is encoded at the strain level and calls for future analytical methods to explore individual-specific microbial diversity at that resolution, acknowledging that current methodology generally lacks the ability to characterize microbiome features at the immunological interface or strain level in this context.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use this material to establish the current state of evidence: species-level associations in human ICI cohorts and strain-level mechanistic validation in preclinical models. Cite the Pal et al. trial as evidence that specific strains can influence ICI outcomes in humans, but explicitly note the methodological gap regarding strain-level baseline prediction in human cohorts. Use the mechanistic details (immune cell changes, cytokines) to support the biological plausibility of strain-specific effects. Highlight the reliance on 16S sequencing in existing human studies as a limitation that necessitates the proposed strain-level validation gap.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The specific success criterion requires human cohort studies using strain-level resolution (metagenomics/culturomics) for ICI prediction. The human studies cited in this material relied on 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, which typically resolves to genus or species level, not strain level. The strain-specific functional validation described was conducted in mouse models, not human cohorts. The human intervention trial (CBM588) validates strain-specific function therapeutically but does not represent a baseline prediction study using strain-resolved microbiome profiling.
useful_material: This review summarizes human clinical correlations between Bifidobacterium abundance and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) outcomes, specifically citing a 2018 melanoma study (42 patients) and an NSCLC study where responders showed higher Bifidobacterium levels via 16S sequencing. It details a human intervention trial (Pal et al., metastatic renal cell carcinoma) where a specific probiotic strain (CBM588) combined with nivolumab/ipilimumab significantly improved progression-free survival and response rates compared to ICI alone. Additionally, it reports preclinical strain-level differentiation, noting that among four Bifidobacterium strains tested in mice, only specific strains (B.bif_K57, B.bif_K18) synergized with PD-1 inhibitors, while others (B.bif_B06) did not, linked to differences in immune cell infiltration (CD8+ T cells, NK cells) and cytokine profiles (IFN-γ, IL-2).

This study reviews clinical trials investigating defined bacterial isolates and consortia for ICI modulation, listing specific strain-level interventions such as Bifidobacterium animalis lactis (EDP1503) and Clostridium butyricum (CBM 588) with associated NCT numbers (e.g., NCT03595683, NCT03829111). The authors explicitly state that while species-level associations (e.g., Bifidobacterium longum) exist, the signature of favorable bacterial strains based on sequencing has not been consistent across patient studies, and questions remain regarding which assay (metagenomics, culturomics) is ideal to identify specific bacteria. The text notes that clinical trials are ongoing to determine if single bacterial interventions improve antitumor immunity, but confirms that predicting clinical outcomes from specific strains is yet to be determined.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as the primary evidence for the existence of human clinical data supporting strain-level over species-level resolution for ICI prediction. Use the specific strain examples (Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium) to illustrate intraspecies functional divergence. Highlight the regimen-specificity finding as a critical condition for interpreting strain biomarkers. Note the lack of experimental functional validation as a limitation when discussing mechanistic certainty.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: While this study fulfills the criterion of finding a human cohort using strain-level resolution linked to ICI outcomes, it does not experimentally validate the microbial functions themselves (e.g., via culturomics, gnotobiotic models, or metabolite measurement) to confirm causality. The functional claims rely on genomic potential inference. Additionally, the external validation was primarily limited to melanoma cohorts for the meta-analysis, and the 'pan-cancer' claim is based on internal rare cancer subtypes.
useful_material: This study performed deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing on baseline fecal samples from a human phase 2 clinical trial cohort (CA209-538, n=106) and a meta-analysis of six external studies (n=364) to link strain-resolved microbial abundances to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) outcomes. The authors constructed a custom strain reference database (1,397 genomes) and demonstrated that strain-level resolution significantly improved machine learning prediction of response and progression-free survival compared to species-level quantification. Specific strain distinctions were highlighted, such as Faecalibacterium strains (positive association) versus Bifidobacterium dentium (negative) compared to Bifidobacterium longum (positive), and Akkermansia muciniphila versus A. muciniphila B. The study also identified genomic functional potentials, noting that positive Ruminococcaceae strains possessed complete acetyl-CoA butyrate pathways while negative ones did not. Furthermore, it established that strain-response signatures are ICB regimen-specific (valid for combination anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 but not anti-PD-1 monotherapy).

This study conducted a prospective observational cohort study (NCT05102773) of metastatic melanoma patients (n=41 assessable) receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), using metagenomic whole-genome shotgun sequencing (MetaPhlAn4/HUMAnN3) to link baseline gut microbiome composition to treatment response (RECIST v1.1) and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The authors identified specific taxa associated with outcomes, such as Intestinimonas butyriciproducens and Blautia luti with response, and Bifidobacterium dentium with irAEs. The study explicitly notes that while WGS was used, the design establishes association rather than causality or functional validation, and results are primarily reported at the species or genus level (e.g., Lachnospiraceae family, Blautia spp.), with limited strain-level differentiation (e.g., Lachnospira sp. NSJ 43) without functional characterization of those strains.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Use the mechanistic details (A2A receptor signaling, T-cell metabolic support) to justify the hypothesis for the planned human quantification study. Cite the explicit statement regarding the lack of human tumor concentration data to reinforce the gap's significance. Search for the primary references cited for the mouse immunotherapy data (e.g., Mager et al., Science 2020) to verify if any human cohort analysis was omitted in this review. Prioritize searching clinical trial registries or metabolomic datasets from ICI trials that may have measured purine metabolites in biofluids or tissue biopsies.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The specific success criterion of identifying prospective human studies reporting absolute concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or SCFAs in paired tumor tissue and serum/stool from ICI-treated solid tumor patients remains unaddressed. This study explicitly states that human studies on inosine have been limited to urate-elevating properties and that findings from animal models regarding immunotherapy efficacy need to be translated to humans. No quantitative data on intratumoral inosine levels in cancer patients correlating with ICI response is provided.
useful_material: This study details the mechanistic pathway by which gut microbiota-derived inosine enhances immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) efficacy, specifically identifying Bifidobacterium pseudolongum as an inosine-producing bacterium that acts through adenosine A2A receptors on tumor-infiltrating T lymphocytes. It explains that inosine serves as an alternative carbon source for CD8+ T-cell function under glucose restriction and has a significantly longer half-life (15 h) than adenosine (~5 s), making it a stable signaling molecule in the microenvironment. The authors distinguish inosine's direct immunomodulatory effects from downstream urate effects, providing a biological rationale for quantifying inosine specifically rather than general purine metabolites.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Retrieve the primary studies cited in Section 6.3 (e.g., references 182, 184) to determine if they contain intratumoral metabolite quantification. Conduct a targeted search for metabolomics studies specifically profiling the tumor microenvironment in ICI-treated patients, focusing on methodologies that report absolute concentration units in tissue biopsies alongside peripheral samples.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: This review does not report absolute physiological concentrations (e.g., μmol/g or μM) of inosine or SCFAs inside the human tumor microenvironment. It references associations in plasma and fecal samples but does not describe paired tumor tissue and serum/stool measurements from prospective human studies with specific quantitative data. The success criterion requiring identified prospective human studies with absolute tissue concentrations remains open.
useful_material: Section 6.3 identifies microbiome-derived metabolites, specifically short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and inosine, as candidate blood-accessible biomarkers associated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor outcomes. The authors note that higher concentrations of fecal and plasma SCFAs were associated with longer progression-free survival in patients treated with nivolumab or pembrolizumab, and preclinical studies suggest inosine enhances checkpoint blockade response. The text explicitly categorizes these markers as exploratory, highlighting confounding factors such as diet, antibiotic exposure, geography, and host metabolism that influence circulating metabolite concentrations.
Explicit statement that human studies reporting spatial redistribution of inosine across intestinal compartments are currently missing, with most data derived from bulk metabolomic analysis.
Statement that no human studies have longitudinally tracked inosine levels or purine metabolic flux from colitis through dysplasia to established CRC.

Reference to a Phase-2 clinical trial (n=172 mixed solid tumors) evaluating inosine (0.2 g orally three times/day) as an adjunct to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors and chemotherapy, noting mild efficacy enhancement but lacking separate CRC-specific reporting (n=10 within digestive system group n=55).

Mechanistic evidence from preclinical models (germ-free mice, MC38/CT26 cells) showing microbial inosine (e.g., from Bifidobacterium pseudolongum) enhances ICI efficacy via A2A receptor-dependent T cell activation and IFN-γ release.

Description of inosine's dual role: promoting anti-tumor immunity (Th1 differentiation, M1 macrophage polarization) versus supporting tumor metabolism (alternative carbon source, EMT promotion via LACC1 enzyme).
Identification of specific inosine-producing taxa (Bifidobacterium pseudolongum, Lactobacillus johnsonii/reuteri) and host enzymes (ADA, LACC1) regulating inosine availability.

This study identifies inosine and short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) as key microbiota-derived metabolites influencing immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response. It reports that Bifidobacterium pseudolongum-derived inosine improves antitumor actions via activation of adenosine A2A receptors on T cells, citing preclinical evidence (Mager et al. 2020). For SCFAs, it notes that increased fecal propionic acid in anti-PD-1 patients correlates with increased antitumor responses and prolonged survival (Botticelli et al. 2020), while increased serum butyrate in anti-CTLA-4 patients links to poor outcomes (Coutzac et al. 2020a, b). Mechanisms described include SCFA-mediated histone deacetylase (HDAC) suppression and G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) activation. The text distinguishes between metabolite effects in different treatment contexts (anti-PD-1 vs. anti-CTLA-4) and compartments (fecal vs. serum).

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Cite this study as evidence for systemic and gut-level SCFA quantification correlating with ICI response in humans, specifically noting the absolute concentrations in stool and plasma. Explicitly state that intratumoral concentrations were not measured. Use the mechanistic discussion to support the biological plausibility of SCFA influence on immunity, while distinguishing between the study's observational associations and the unverified mechanistic claims. Continue searching for studies that include paired tumor tissue biopsies for metabolite analysis to fulfill the intratumoral criterion.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: This study does not measure metabolite concentrations inside the human tumour microenvironment (intratumoral tissue), which is the primary requirement of the gap question. It only provides data for fecal and plasma compartments. Additionally, the study does not report measurements for inosine. The correlation between fecal/plasma SCFA levels and actual intratumoral concentrations remains unestablished by this material.
useful_material: This prospective cohort study (n=52) measured absolute concentrations of specific short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in fecal and plasma samples from solid tumor patients treated with PD-1 inhibitors (nivolumab or pembrolizumab). Fecal samples were analyzed for acetic acid (AA), propionic acid (PA), butyric acid (BA), valeric acid (VA), and others, reported in μmol/g (e.g., median fecal PA: 172.6 μmol/g in responders vs 103.6 μmol/g in nonresponders). Plasma samples were analyzed for SCFAs including isovaleric acid (IVA), reported in μmol/g (e.g., median plasma IVA: 0.3 μmol/g in responders vs 0.0 μmol/g in nonresponders). High concentrations of fecal AA, PA, BA, VA and plasma IVA were significantly associated with longer progression-free survival (e.g., fecal PA HR 0.08, 95% CI 0.03-0.20). The study also identified dietary associations, where high frequency of mushroom intake correlated with higher fecal BA and VA and longer progression-free survival.

This study is a narrative review that details the mechanistic axes by which gut microbial metabolites, specifically short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), modulate the tumor microenvironment (TME) and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) response. The authors describe SCFA mechanisms including G-protein-coupled receptor binding (GPR41, GPR43, GPR109a) and histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibition, which affect T-cell exhaustion and macrophage polarization. Crucially, the authors explicitly state that while physiological mucosal concentrations favor regulatory T-cell induction, the concentration-response relationship in human tumor-bearing contexts has not been characterized. The review summarizes landmark clinical studies linking microbial composition to ICI outcomes but notes these rely on 16S rRNA or metagenomics rather than metabolomic quantification. Inosine is not discussed in the supplied text.

This study identifies specific microbial metabolites mechanistically linked to ICI response, including inosine (via Bifidobacterium pseudolongum and A2A receptor on CD8+ T cells) and short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate affecting dendritic cells and T-cell memory).

The authors report that metabolomic profiling in dietary fiber studies demonstrated higher fecal butyrate and acetate levels correlating with greater intratumoral T-cell infiltration, though absolute tumor tissue concentrations were not specified in this text.

This review notes that three metabolomic studies integrated microbiome and metabolite data to predict treatment outcomes (specifically adverse events with AUC 0.963 using fecal and plasma profiles), indicating the existence of quantitative metabolite datasets in the field.

The discussion highlights the complexity of metabolite stoichiometry and immune contexture, noting that high concentrations of butyrate can suppress IL-2-dependent memory formation while acetate/propionate enhance dendritic cell fitness.

fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: ['Cite this study as the primary example of moving from human metagenomic association to experimental strain-level functional validation in the context of ICI.', 'Use the SagA/Nod2 mechanism to illustrate how specific bacterial molecules (rather than whole taxa) can be identified and validated as therapeutic adjuvants.', 'Contrast the engineered strain results (E. faecalis-sagA) with wild-type strains to highlight the importance of functional gene presence over taxonomic identity in predicting ICI response.', 'Note the limitation that validation is preclinical (mouse models) and that direct patient-strain-to-mouse transfer was not explicitly described, distinguishing this from culturomics studies that isolate patient-specific strains.']
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: ['While this study validates Enterococcus strains, it does not validate other ICI-associated strains (e.g., Bifidobacterium, Akkermansia) identified in different human cohorts, leaving the broader landscape of strain-level validation incomplete.', 'The strains tested were human-commensal isolates (e.g., Com15) rather than strains directly isolated from specific ICI responder patients in a matched cohort-to-model transfer design.', 'Experimental validation is confined to mouse models; there is no direct experimental validation of these specific strain functions in human clinical trials within this material.']
useful_material: This study experimentally validates the function of ICI-associated bacterial strains (Enterococcus genus) using gnotobiotic and antibiotic-pretreated mouse tumor models (B16-F10 melanoma, MC38, MCA205).

Specific human-commensal strains (e.g., E. faecium Com15) were orally administered to mice and shown to significantly enhance anti-PD-L1, anti-PD-1, and anti-CTLA-4 efficacy compared to non-protective strains (e.g., E. faecalis OG1RF).

The study distinguishes genomic potential from functional validation by identifying the SagA peptidoglycan hydrolase gene, confirming its enzymatic activity in vitro, and proving sufficiency via heterologous expression in E. faecalis and Lactococcus lactis.

Functional validation included metabolite measurement/administration: synthetic Nod2-active muropeptides (MDP-L,D) replicated the antitumor effect, confirming the molecular mechanism beyond live bacterial colonization.
Mechanistic validation established host dependency: the antitumor effect was abrogated in Nod2-/- mice, confirming the specific host receptor pathway required for the strain's function.

This study experimentally validates the functional capacity of responder versus non-responder gut microbiota communities using fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) into gnotobiotic mice, demonstrating that responder microbiota decreases tumor growth following ICI treatment. It identifies specific Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs) belonging to genera such as Colidextribacter, Frisingicoccus, Marvinbryantia, and Blautia that overlap between human responders and colonized mice, correlating with tumor size. Crucially for the gap, the authors explicitly state in the Conclusions and Discussion that 'The role of isolate-specific function... has been underappreciated' and that the work 'supports further investigation using isolate-driven models,' indicating that isolation and validation of specific strains from these ASVs had not been performed in this study and remains a necessary future step.

The review explicitly distinguishes between human observational associations and preclinical experimental validation. It documents that while fecal transplantation from human responders to mice recapitulates outcomes (e.g., references [19–21]), these studies often 'did not further identify the specific bacteria whose abundance was associated with immune responses' and highlights the need for 'inoculation with single-lineage bacteria.' It lists specific genera validated in preclinical models via oral gavage (e.g., Bifidobacterium spp., Bacteroides fragilis, Akkermansia muciniphila, Enterococcus hirae) but notes inconsistencies when compared to human cohort data (e.g., Bacteroidales associated with response in some studies, non-response in others). The text explicitly states that 'improvements in the isolation of cultivable bacteria and derivation of individual clones... may represent future steps,' indicating that comprehensive strain-level experimental validation linked to human cohorts is currently lacking or incomplete.

research_question: How does the gut microbiome modulate the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors in solid tumours, and what mechanisms mediate that effect?

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者清晰区分微生物组 -ICI 互作中的观察性关联与干预性因果信号，理解抗生素使用时机（特别是 ICI 启动后 60 天内）与肿瘤类型对疗效影响的异质性，评估 FMT/LBP 在真实世界中的获益/风险比，并明确当前领域缺乏 III 期 RCT 的证据边界及未来优先事项。
shared_outline.scope: 临床证据表明，肠道微生物群扰动（尤其是抗生素与质子泵抑制剂暴露）与实体瘤患者免疫检查点抑制剂（ICI）生存期缩短存在稳健的时序依赖性负相关，其中 ICI 启动后 60 天内的暴露风险最高（HR 1.27），且该效应在头颈部癌、肾细胞癌和乳腺癌中显著，而在肺癌和黑色素瘤中未达统计学显著；粪菌移植（FMT）与活体生物疗法（LBP）在早期临床试验中展现出概念验证潜力（NSCLC ORR 80%, 黑色素瘤 ORR 75%），但伴随显著的毒性信号（双药方案下 65% 发生 3 级+irAE）与供体/患者选择异质性。当前证据层级呈现明显分化：大样本回顾性队列提供了高置信度的预后关联，而干预性数据仍局限于单臂 II 期试验，缺乏随机对照与长期安全性确证。因此，临床转化准备度目前仅支持基于观察性数据的抗生素管理建议，FMT/LBP 等靶向干预仍需等待 III 期随机对照试验验证。
shared_outline.title: 临床证据格局：抗生素时机、FMT 试验与观察性数据

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者掌握预测 ICI 疗效的核心微生物特征清单，理解分类学特征与代谢物在预测效力上的差异，明确当前生物标志物研究的证据层级（观察性关联 vs. 定量验证），并识别限制其临床转化的关键方法学与生物学边界。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群通过特定的分类学特征（门/属/种/株）与代谢物谱（SCFAs、肌苷等）系统性调节实体瘤 ICI 疗效，但现有证据呈现高度的情境依赖性（癌种、治疗方案、宿主背景）。观察性关联已确立特定菌群与代谢物的预后价值，而定量代谢组学与菌株分辨率研究正推动生物标志物从“物种丰度”向“功能通路”演进；然而，人类肿瘤微环境内代谢物绝对浓度的缺失及跨队列泛化能力的不足，限制了其作为独立临床决策工具的转化就绪度。
shared_outline.title: 微生物特征：预测 ICI 反应的菌分类群与代谢物

shared_outline.purpose: 使读者清晰理解微生物群调制 ICI 疗效的三大核心生物学路径，掌握关键菌种/代谢物的作用靶点与浓度阈值，并能准确评估临床前因果证据与人类观察性数据的证据等级差异，从而在撰写综述时合理界定机制假设与确证事实的边界。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群通过免疫启动（DC/T 细胞互作）、代谢物信号（SCFAs、肌苷、色氨酸/胆汁酸受体通路）及屏障完整性/细菌易位三大路径调制实体瘤 ICI 疗效；临床前模型确立了明确的因果链条，但人类数据多为观察性关联，需严格区分物种差异与肿瘤类型特异性，避免将动物模型结论直接外推为临床事实。肌苷等关键代谢物的人类肿瘤微环境浓度数据尚缺，现有证据主要依赖血浆相关性与小鼠模型。
shared_outline.title: 机制通路：免疫、代谢与屏障功能的介导作用

shared_outline.purpose: 帮助肿瘤临床医生与研究者区分已验证的临床信号与探索性策略，掌握不同干预手段（FMT、LBP、饮食）的适用人群、安全边界及机制依据，为参与或设计下一代微生物组-ICI 联合试验提供决策参考。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群干预（FMT、活体生物药/LBP、饮食与代谢物）在增强实体瘤 ICI 疗效方面展现出明确的生物学合理性与初步临床信号，但其临床可靠性受限于供体/菌株异质性、irAE 风险交互作用及缺乏 III 期确证数据。FMT 疗效高度依赖肿瘤类型与 ICI 方案背景（一线单药 vs 耐药挽救），当前证据支持将抗生素管理作为常规实践，而 FMT 与精准菌群工程需严格限定于临床试验或特定难治情境，尚未达到常规临床推荐标准。
shared_outline.title: 治疗干预：FMT、益生菌与饮食调节的可行性

shared_outline.purpose: 帮助读者系统理解当前微生物组-ICI 互作证据的证据等级差异，识别导致结果不一致的方法学与生物学根源，明确区分已验证的临床限制与待探索的机制缺口，并掌握基于证据等级的研究优先事项与转化路线图。
shared_outline.scope: 肠道微生物群对实体瘤 ICI 疗效的调节作用具有坚实的生物学合理性，但现有证据呈现显著的层级分化：观察性关联（如抗生素暴露、特定菌属富集）提供了稳健的效应信号，而干预性证据（如 FMT、活体生物制品）仍局限于早期试验且伴随定植不确定性与安全性考量；跨队列生物标志物难以复现主要源于方法学异质性（测序平台、生信流程、样本采集时序）与生物学情境依赖性（肿瘤类型、宿主基线、给药时序）。系统性检索确认当前无已完成的大规模纯微生物干预 III 期 RCT，TACITO 等试验为 II 期设计且未正式达到主要终点。未来转化需从"单一物种分类学"转向"功能代谢通路"，并依托标准化多中心 RCT 与空间多组学技术，以建立可重复的预测模型与精准干预路径。
